free_tier.stated: no free tier; this is the cheapest plan in the store at USD 9.88 a year

retention.stated: the disk persists while the annual plan is paid; no deletion policy for non-payment is stated on the order form

egress.terms: 2 TB a month, stated on the order form as '2 TB Bandwidth' on a '1 Gbps Network Port'

interface_detail: KVM with root; the order form carries a full OS picker (AlmaLinux, Rocky, CentOS, Debian, Ubuntu) and asks for a hostname and a root password
tooling: any SSH client; the Virtualizor panel
chaining: the cheapest row in the corpus with a dedicated IPv4 and 2 GiB of RAM: USD 0.82 a month buys a real KVM guest with 30 GB of disk, enough to be a daily-driver side box, a WireGuard node or a monitor that answers on a routable address
binding_note: 2 TB is generous against 30 GB of disk and 1 vCore, so the single vCore is what a real workload meets first; there is no published overage price.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: the order form was read to the configuration step, which asks only for a hostname, a root password and an OS, and it states no card, no hold and no identity document. The vendor names Stripe and Alipay on its payment page. Whether the checkout then demands a card, and whether a debit or prepaid card is accepted, was not reached because reaching it would mean placing an order.

reliability_note: no reliability event observed the order form renders and prices normally
confidence_note: read in a real browser on the vendor's own configured product page after the operator cleared the Cloudflare challenge: the order summary prints the plan name, the annual price and 'Total Due Today'

evidence.proved: the rendered order summary reads 'Promo VPS Special NY | PROMO VPS NY | Promo VPS Special NY $9.88 USD', 'Setup Fees: $0.00 USD', 'Annually: $9.88 USD', '$9.88 USD Total Due Today', with 'Choose Billing Cycle: $9.88 USD Annually'
the plan specification on the same form reads '2 GB RAM', '1x vCore CPU', '30 GB SSD', '2 TB Bandwidth', '1 Gbps Network Port', '1 IPv4'
the category page advertises the same SKU as 'Promo VPS Special NY ... Starting from $9.88 USD Annually'

notes: DediRock's Black Friday page (dedirock.com/black-friday/) advertises a USD 9.88/yr Saver but its own Order Now href (store/promo-vp/promo-vps-saver-ny-bf) lands on a category listing whose cheapest line is USD 5.99 a MONTH for a different shape. That is a dead link. The standing promo SKU at store/promo-vp/promo-vps-special-ny is a different product and it does sell, at USD 9.88 a year, which the browser render above confirms. Both facts are true at once: the seasonal page is a fossil and the cheap SKU it made famous is alive at a URL the seasonal page never links to.

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 9.88 a year divided by 12 = USD 0.8233 a month, paid once as USD 9.88 out of pocket
extras.renewal_note: the order form states the annual price and says nothing about what year two costs; the earlier BF page's prices are not a renewal statement
extras.stock: in stock: the form rendered a configurator with an OS picker and no sold-out notice
extras.payment_methods: Stripe and Alipay named on the vendor's payment page; not reached at checkout
